newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Nov 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A report from Independent Shareholder Services, a specialist corporate governance advisory firm, advises Coles Myer institutional shareholders to vote against the re-election of Solomon Lew and Nick Greiner as directors at Coles Myer's annual meeting on Nvember 19, because of poor disclosure of their role in the controversial Yannon transaction. Page 1.

Many big market-linked superannuation funds have delivered a compound annual return over the past 10 years of 9.6 percent less than the 10.9 percent produced by cash, according to a performance survey issued by InTech Asset Consulting. InTech managing director Ron Liling said the relative performance of funds with a substantial exposure to the sharemarket was likely to deteriorate further in coming months. Page 1.

Environment Minister Robert Hill yesterday gave approval to Korea Zinc Australia Ltd's A$500 million zinc refining and smelting operation in Townsville and signed an agreement with Tasmania outlining the environmental impact assessment process for the proposed A$1.2 billion Taiwan Pulp and Paper Corporation mill project in northern Tasmania. Meanwhile, Access Economics released a report which revealed mining and resource processing projects, both committed and under consideration, increased by about A$29 billion or 45 percent over the 12 months to September. Page 2.

In a blow to Australian National Industries' bid to sell its Holter operations, Saarberg yesterday informed the company that it would sell back to ANI its 50 percent interest in the Saarberg-Holter Wassertechnik waste-water treatment business. ANI will ow hold 100 percent of SHW, which has a total book value of A$106 million. Page 35.

Furniture and homeware retailer Freedom Furniture yesterday announced a net profit for the year to September of A$3.3 million - 18 percent higher than forecast in its prospectus. Managing director Jonathon Pinshaw said Freedom was able to increase its margins during the year through cost-cutting and higher prices. Page 36.

Foodland Associated Ltd's total group sales during the September quarter were down 0.2 percent on the previous corresponding quarter from A$876.68 million. The group's general manager of finance, Chris Bennett, said the decline was attributable to poor etailing conditions leading up to the New Zealand parliamentary elections and high domestic interest rates. Page 36.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Chairman of giant retailer Coles Myer, Nobby Clark, has rebuffed board hopeful Peter Willcocks' request for greater disclosure about the group's troubled Yannon transaction and other matters. Willcocks, who for a second time has nominated for a board seat, said he will be vigorously pursuing matters at Coles' annual meeting on November 19. Page 21.

National Australia Bank Ltd has revealed plans which will place the banking giant at the forefront of international securities trading, following the purchase of a local electronic trading service, Ausmaq Ltd, for an undisclosed amount. The bank intends Ausmaq to provide an international global trading forum where investors can place funds virtually anywhere in the world. Page 21.

As part of a joint venture to provide a worldwide Internet advertising company, pay TV group British Sky Broadcasting has taken an option to buy 15 percent of Internet service provider OzEmail Ltd. The deal values OzEmail at A$235 million, but does not give BSkyB a seat in the boardroom. The new company - Web Wide Media - will focus on selling advertising on Internet sites. Page 21.

Sky wars appear imminent as Qantas yesterday rejected a request from its landlord - the Federal Airports Corp - to provide aspiring domestic airline, Aussie Airlines, with space at domestic terminals. The FAC has served notice on Qantas, giving the airline four-weeks to reach a sub-lease agreement with Aussie. Page 23.

Engineering and metals group Australian National Industries Ltd has been forced to buy back a half-share of its German environmental engineering project at a cost of A$55 million. German Government-owned Saarberg, a partner in the waste water treatment pant, exercised a put option on the stake which forced the ANI buyback. Page 23.

Regional pay TV operator Austar yesterday joined the queue to become the fourth company to launch a legal challenge to the alliance between fellow operators Australis Media and Optus Vision. Austar claims the three-month-old alliance contravenes its own agreement with Australis. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian National Industries has been forced to buy back a German environmental waste control business at a cost of A$55 million. German Government-owned Saarberg has enforced an option which will see a 50 percent stake in the waste water treatment busness go back to ANI. Page 21.

Coles Myer chairman Nobby Clark yesterday defended the group's largest shareholder, Solomon Lew, by rejecting claims from board candidate Peter Willcocks that the retailing giant was breaching its own corporate guidelines by supporting Lew's re-election as a director. Page 21.

The future structure of the Ten Group will become clearer today following the expiry of pre-emptive rights to John Singleton Advertising's JSA.AX A$60 million shareholding by other shareholders. CanWest Global Communications CWW.TO, which has a 57.5 percent economic interest and a 15 percent voting interest in Ten, has been trying to set up a vehicle to buy the Singleton shares as it is prohibited from buying more shares in the network, being a foreign company. Page 23.

Australia's largest Internet service provider OzEmail has signed a joint venture with European pay TV group British Sky Broadcasting take on the global Internet advertising market, in a deal which will see the two groups hold equal shares in the joint ventures. OzEmail has agreed to issue BSkyB two-year options over about 15 percent of its capital at a price of A$17.60 a share. Page 23.

Defying the weak retail market, newly-listed furniture retailer Freedom Furniture has achieved an annual profit, before abnormal items, of A$6.1 million - 10 percent above the prospectus forecast of A$5.5 million. Managing director Jonathan Pinshaw said he retailer was in for further growth following the 0.5 percent reduction in interest rates. Page 25.

Cairn Energy's A$365 million takeover of Command Petroleum came closer to finalisation yesterday after U.S.-based Snyder Oil Corp accepted the offer from the UK oil and gas independent for its 32.6 percent holding in Command. Snyder president Thomas Edelmn said his company was anticipating the merged group having the potential to triple its value within three years because of its unique position in the oil and gas sector of the Indian sub-continent. Page 25.
THE AGE

Responding to questions by independent board candidate Peter Willcocks, Coles Myer chairman Nobby Clark rejected claims the company had breached corporate governance guidelines by supporting Solomon Lew's re-election as a director, saying Lew was not compromised "simply because there is a significant supplier relationship with the company". Page C1.

The ANZ Bank is seeking a new advertising agency for its A$20 million retail advertising account after sacking the Campaign Palace after five years. In a statement ANZ said the advertising account review was designed to build on the bank's long-term bran positioning. Page C1.

Reef Mining NL announced yesterday that 568 ounces of refined gold was produced from the South Poverty reef in the Tarnagulla goldfield in central Victoria last month. Marking the first return from its A$7.3 million expenditure on the redevelopment of the gold field, Reef made A$271,450 in sales for the month. Page C1.

Australian National Industries chief executive Peter Stancliffe said last night the company hoped to secure a higher sale price for the Saarberg-Hoelter Wassertechnik (SHW) waste water treatment business now that it had full control once again, after the German government-owned Saarberg enforced an option to make ANI pay A$55 million for a 50 percent stake in the business. Page C3.

Following Southcorp's recent announcement that it would spend A$100 million in the next three years on vineyard development and wine processing upgrades, executive general manager of wine operations, Brian Johnston, announced yesterday Australia's largest wine group would spend A$35 million on its South Australian and Victorian bottling lines to boost its wine output in Australia and overseas. Page C3.

Releasing the Australian Securities Commission's annual report yesterday, chairman Alan Cameron said the commission had a successful year in enforcing improved standards in business, with 19 corporate criminals jailed, 24 criminal convictions secured and 31 major cases prosecuted. Cameron said the ASC has recovered A$16 million for creditors and investors through its enforcement actions. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
